en: I worship within my heart Lord Bhairava—the one who has pervaded the specific distinctions of all moving and unmoving beings, who is consciousness, singular, infinite, and beginningless, and who is the refuge for the helpless—by means of a mind that is identical with you. 1.
Now, through the power of your grace, this entire universe appears to me as consisting of you;
and since you, O Great Lord, are forever my very self, everything is for me composed of your own self.

Since You, the Lord who encompasses the universe, are one's own self, there is no talk of fear regarding the cycle of existence, even though the multitudes of karmas exist which produce unbearable suffering, delusion, and terror. // 3 //
O Antaka, do not cast this gaze upon me, so exceedingly fierce with wrath;
for I am steadfast through meditation on the service of Śaṅkara, and I consist of the terrifying power of Bhairava.

O Lord, thus, with the thick darkness shattered by the rays of consciousness consisting of the Supreme Being that have arisen within me, I shall never again fear the goblins of death, Yama, the Ender, and karma; homage be to You! 5.

Having perceived the true nature of all things in the universe through the rays of the awakening of the manifested Truth, I attain bliss in You, my own Self, who are completely filled with the supreme nectar of existence. 6.

O Lord, the very moment that state of affliction which inflicts intense torment comes within the range of my mind, at that very moment there rises for me a rain of the nectar of your non-dual hymn of praise.
O Śaṅkara, this is true: vows, gifts, ritual baths, and austerities tear asunder the heat of worldly existence;
yet it is contemplation on the supreme nectar of your scripture that pours forth a stream of bliss within the mind.
This consciousness of mine dances, sings, and rejoices intensely, O Lord Bhairava,
having attained you— the beloved, the singular Sudarśana, who is difficult for other people to find and who knows the sacred tradition (samaya).
Abhinavagupta composed this hymn on the tenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Pauṣa, in the year 84 [of the Vikrama era].
By means of which the compassionate Lord instantly pacifies the torment of the desert of existence for all people.
This hymn, consisting of nine verses and titled "The New," is completed.
